design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 0 (medical_transportation_benefits, category ride)

[1] Why this is a good test. The member asks one thing: have the money for her September radiation trip put on her RideLink prepaid card. Nothing for that trip is on the ledger, so a correct seat must (a) read the settlement rule and see that a trip settlement is not released until the ledger carries the trip's approved mileage entry, (b) read the mileage rule and see that for a trip whose return leg is on a later date the mileage entry is fixed only after the trip's lodging and meals entry stands, (c) work out three multi-factor amounts in that order on the world as it stands at each write, and (d) hand the payout to the member. The difficulty is reading prerequisite sentences, reconciling ride legs, ledger history and two other products' records (plan claims/membership, equipment authorization), and exact arithmetic; there is one tool per problem, so nothing is gained by guessing tools.

[2] Scope snapshot (Step 0). Draw printed by scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0: {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4]}. Assignment: ride_ext_stay_lodging_meals = 6 factors, ride_ext_trip_mileage = 4, ride_ext_trip_settlement = 4. Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: the Mileage Reimbursement chain — lodging and meals approval, mileage approval, trip settlement payout (events ride_mileage_approved for types lodging_meals and mileage, ride_mileage_paid) and tools approve_stay_lodging_meals_3bb3a021, approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186, collect_trip_settlement_816cec94. Reserved for task 1 (draw 2 prerequisites, factor counts [5,4,6]): the value-added allotment ledger (previous-year expiry, new-year load) and the late-pickup alternative ride (ride_mileage_approved type late_pickup_alternative), none of which this task touches.

[3] Policies, lineage, trigger. ride_ext_stay_lodging_meals (state_due; subject ride_mileage_approved; base_policy_refs ride_late_pickup_policy, ride_mileage_reimbursement, ride_long_distance; overwrite: ride_long_distance 'For an approved long-distance trip ... lodging up to lodging_per_night_usd per night and meals up to meals_per_day_usd per travel day are reimbursed as a lodging_meals reimbursement.' -> 'Lodging and meals on such a stay are paid as the allowances this rule sets out, whatever the receipts show.' because the course meals rate plus supplement exceed the base 'up to 25.00'). ride_ext_trip_mileage (state_due; same subject and lineage; overwrite of ride_mileage_reimbursement's first sentence 'Mileage is reimbursed only on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement, ... at mileage_rate_usd per approved mile measured by mileage_distance_basis for the round trip.' -> 'Mileage is reimbursed only on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement, for a trip registered with a trip number before the appointment, on the approved miles and at the per-mile rate and taper this rule sets out.', keeping the level and registration conditions verbatim). ride_ext_trip_settlement (on_request; subject ride_mileage_paid; base ride_mileage_reimbursement; overwrite 'an approved amount is paid within mileage_payment_days by the member's chosen payment method' -> 'A trip settlement pays the approved amounts together with any late-settlement credit and allowance this rule sets out, to the payment method the member chooses.'). No base eligibility gate is retired: filing_window and one_claim_per_leg stay in force and are inherited into base_preconditions of steps 9 and 11; ride_mileage_paid has no structured gate (policy_scope).

[4] Factor card (tier taken in this world / evidence rows / baseline figure from the Step 5 run).
 ride_ext_stay_lodging_meals (gold 1811.25, all-baseline 1235.00):
  - stay_nights_counted (parameter; multi-source: outbound time AND return time): outbound RL-5541907 07:45 < 09:00, return 14:45 not >= 15:00 (near-miss by 15 minutes) -> exactly one -> 11+1 = 12 nights; baseline 11 nights -> 1670.75. Rows: ride_trips 02611ae0 (outbound), de44f83f (return).
  - stay_length_lodging_taper (method): 11 nights between the appointment dates in [7, 28) -> two-band taper: 7 x 85.00 + 5 x 72.00 = 955.00; baseline flat 12 x 85.00 -> 1876.25.
  - drive_length_edge_day_share (parameter): longest leg of RL-5541907 218.4 miles in [150, 300) -> 0.75; baseline 1 -> 1845.50.
  - treatment_course_meals_rate (parameter; multi-source; cross-difficulty plan): purpose radiation AND 10 paid outpatient hospital claims 2026-09-14..2026-09-25 (plan_claims 81862323 ... a8cb19b5) within three months -> 31.00; near-miss C26-0824-43577 (2026-08-24) is three whole months before 2026-11-25 and falls outside; baseline 25.00 -> 1661.25.
  - income_meal_supplement (parameter; cross-difficulty plan): plan_memberships 87e08e1f income_pct_fpl 74 in (50, 100] -> 3.25; baseline 0 -> 1730.00.
  - attendant_meals_share (parameter; multi-source; cross-difficulty auth): auth 680ae201 (K0001, approved) AND category Prairie Ridge ABD Care -> 1.0; the expired E0601 CPAP auth e6cb128e is the near-miss (not a wheelchair); baseline 0 -> 1383.12.
 ride_ext_trip_mileage (gold 179.66, all-baseline 91.73):
  - chair_treatment_mile_rate (parameter; multi-source; cross-difficulty auth): K0001 approved AND purpose radiation -> 0.32; baseline 0.21 -> 117.90.
  - stay_local_round_trips (method; cross-difficulty plan): lodging entry dated 2026-09-14 (booked at step 9) AND 10 course claims >= 5 -> 10 local round trips; baseline 0 -> 139.78; before step 9 the latest lodging entry (d8748718, 2025-11-17) is the near-miss that does not match the trip.
  - destination_local_miles (parameter): outbound 218.4 >= 200 -> 14.0 per round trip; baseline 0 -> 139.78.
  - approved_miles_taper (method): 576.8 in (500, 1000] -> 500 + 0.8 x 76.8 = 561.44; baseline all miles in full -> 184.58.
 ride_ext_trip_settlement (gold 2035.77, all-baseline 1990.91):
  - late_settlement_credit_rate (parameter): 43 days in (30, 60] -> 0.01; baseline 0 -> 2005.91.
  - settlement_clock_start (method; cross-difficulty plan): latest-service outpatient claim a8cb19b5 (service 2026-09-25) booked 2026-10-13 > return date -> clock 2026-10-13; the return leg was registered 2026-08-31, before the outbound date, so the extended-stay registration tier does not apply; baseline return date 2026-09-25 (61 days -> 0.02) -> 2065.64.
  - stay_length_credit_scale (parameter): lodging entry records 12 nights in [7, 14) -> 1.5; baseline 1 -> 2025.82.
  - late_settlement_allowance (parameter; multi-source; cross-difficulty plan): ABD Care AND income 74 <= 100 -> 15.00; baseline 0 -> 2020.77.
 Every tier condition rests on records (legs, ledger, claims, membership, authorization); no stamp field is read. Per-task floors: multi-source (stay_nights_counted, treatment_course_meals_rate, attendant_meals_share, chair_treatment_mile_rate, late_settlement_allowance) and cross-difficulty (plan, auth) present.

[5] Base-invariant card. Write subject ride_mileage_approved (steps 9, 11): ride_late_pickup_policy (no eligibility; policy_scope: this is not a late_pickup_alternative claim), ride_long_distance (no eligibility; policy_scope: 218.4 one-way miles > 50, registered 2026-08-31 >= 5 business days before 2026-09-14; >= 120-mile lodging threshold), ride_mileage_reimbursement.filing_window (time gate: anchor the trip date ride_trips.appointment_date 2026-09-14, 90 calendar days counted from the day after, inclusive, not_after; last qualifying day 2026-12-13; handling 2026-11-25 is day 72 -> satisfied; just-before/at-boundary cases in temporal_feasibility), ride_mileage_reimbursement.one_claim_per_leg (dedup on trip_number+leg+reimbursement_type: the ledger carries no entry for RL-5541907 of any type, so neither the round_trip lodging_meals nor the round_trip mileage claim is a duplicate). Write subject ride_mileage_paid (step 13): ride_mileage_reimbursement has no gate applying to payments -> policy_scope. The level condition 'only on RideLink Mileage Reimbursement' holds (ride_benefits 56d4e29b variant) and the trip was registered before the appointment (event_date 2026-08-31).

[6] Business-object card. Target object: trip RL-5541907 (legs 02611ae0 outbound 2026-09-14 and de44f83f return 2026-09-25) on active benefit 56d4e29b. Correlation key: trip_number + trip date (claim_trip_date = outbound appointment date). Rows included: the two legs; the ten paid outpatient hospital claims of the course; the new lodging and mileage entries. Rows excluded: RL-5538842 (2025 consult, settled by 243.23 paid 2025-12-05 under MR-251121-3308), RL-5539950 (May 2026 Kearney, 34.58 paid), RL-5541310 (Aug 2026 simulation, 139.78 paid 2026-09-16) — each already settled under its own claim number and trip date, so the settlement's SUM by trip date 2026-09-14 never picks them up. The payment writes back the mileage claim number MR-261125-8057 returned at step 11.

[7] Why each class of seed row exists. customers/plan_memberships: identity + ABD category + income 74 (attendant share, supplement, late allowance). plan_claims: 10 course claims (course meals rate, local round trips, attendance proof, settlement clock via booked 2026-10-13), 2026-08-24 simulation claim (near-miss outside the window; also its own trip's attendance), 2025-11 and 2026-05 claims (attendance for the earlier trips), 2026-08-04 PCP visit (ordinary history). auth: K0001 approved (rate, attendant share), E0601 expired (near-miss). ride_benefits: active Mileage level (rates, thresholds, payment days) and the closed 2019-2023 sedan benefit (history of one-open-benefit rule). ride_trips: four registered trips (8 legs) — the latest pair is the claimed trip; the earlier ones feed the ledger history. ride_ledger: approvals and settlements of the three earlier trips (mileage + lodging for 2025, mileage for May and August 2026) — removing the 2025 lodging row removes the near-miss that makes the mileage prerequisite visible as unmet (the latest lodging entry is another trip); removing the August mileage entry would make the settlement's skip-A world read no mileage at all. Automatic clauses checked: the mileage level has no value-added allotment (no load/expiry obligation), no suspension clause applies (mileage level), nothing is owed at the opening (reimbursement_owed 0.00 = approved 417.59 - paid 417.59), so no other obligation is lit. Cache: reimbursement_owed is left equal to the ledger (no cache trap chosen); the new approvals and payment are ledger rows.

[8] Problem-tree card. Root ride_ext_trip_settlement (owner=user tool collect_trip_settlement_816cec94). Edge 1: settlement -> ride_ext_trip_mileage, kind value_input, gate entries, form state, sentence (negated direction) 'A trip settlement is not released until the ledger carries the approved mileage entry for that trip.', condition: an approved mileage entry for the trip is the latest approved mileage entry; resolved_by approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186 (agent). False at opening: latest approved mileage entry e72c0264 has claim_trip_date 2026-08-24 (RL-5541310). Edge 2: ride_ext_trip_mileage -> ride_ext_stay_lodging_meals, kind value_input, gate local_trips, form state, sentence (affirmative) 'For a trip whose return leg falls on a later date than its outbound leg and whose one-way miles reach the level's lodging threshold, the mileage entry is fixed only after the ledger carries the approved lodging and meals entry for that trip.'; resolved_by approve_stay_lodging_meals_3bb3a021 (agent). False at opening: the only lodging entry d8748718 has claim_trip_date 2025-11-17. Four-point test: both sentences carry an ordering connective (not until / only after) joining this policy's own result to a record-visible state; the state side names ledger entries in the words the ledger lookup shows (approved mileage entry, approved lodging and meals entry) and no action or performer; no tool, id or snake_case token; strength exact (hard requirement, one entry kind each). Direction: a payment is 'not released until' what it waits for stands, a computed entry 'is fixed only after' what it rests on — the charter carries both directions. Unique writer: approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186 is the only tool that books approved mileage entries; approve_stay_lodging_meals_3bb3a021 the only one that books lodging and meals entries. Derivation: sentence + ledger (no entry for the trip) + the other rule ('A trip's mileage entry ... records the trip's reservation number ...' / 'A lodging and meals entry is booked for a registered long-distance trip ...') -> exactly one resolving write each. Topological order: lodging (step 9) -> mileage (step 11) -> settlement (step 13); a chain, so no parallel ordering question. Deletion sensitivity (Step 5 run): skip step 9 -> mileage 139.78 (not 179.66), settlement 156.18; skip step 11 -> settlement 156.18 (not 2035.77). user_scenario names neither prerequisite (see no_user_hint) and the tools check nothing (see tools_do_not_block). No step rests on a real-world wait: the approvals and the payout are synchronous ledger writes; attendance is already proven by paid claims at the opening.

[9] Length and breadth. Depth: payout -> (sentence) mileage entry -> (sentence) lodging entry, each with its own computation. Breadth: legs (dates, times, miles, purpose, registration date), ledger history (latest entries, per-trip SUM), plan claims (course count, window, booked dates), plan membership (category, income), equipment authorization (wheelchair code and status). Removing any factor changes a number (factor card), removing either edge changes a number (tree card).

[10] Where a careless agent goes wrong and how a careful one avoids it: paying from the opening ledger (the latest mileage entry is August's 139.78; the sentence forbids releasing before this trip's entry stands); computing mileage before the lodging entry (no local round trips); counting 11 nights (missing the early-start night) or 13 (treating 14:45 as a late finish); counting the 2026-08-24 simulation claim into the course (it is three whole months back); taking the CPAP authorization as a wheelchair; charging meals in full on the edge days; forgetting the attendant's meals; paying all miles at full rate over 500; starting the settlement clock on the return date (61 days, 2 percent) instead of the claim booked date (43 days, 1 percent); recording the payment under the lodging claim number.

[11] Persona design. Theodora is soft-spoken, tired, courteous ('hon'); opening = surface goal only (radiation trip in Omaha in September, nothing paid, put what is owed on her prepaid card today). Given only when asked: Medicaid ID, DOB, phone, SSN last four, trip details and reservation number, the motel stay and who travelled, the receipts (cannot produce), payment preference. Passive reactions: consents to back-office steps without asking what they are; runs the payout exactly as read to her and reports the screen; accepts the amount; closes after hearing the money went to her card. She never states amounts, nights or rates, and never names mileage or lodging claims. Authority boundary: everything she volunteers matches initial_state (registered at the end of August = event_date 2026-08-31; card used for other trips = prepaid_card payments).

[12] Reachability walk-through (one conversation, frozen 2026-11-25 10:20 CST). Turn 1: member asks for the trip money on her card -> agent asks ID -> find_customers(PR42731608), verify with DOB. Agent reads membership, benefit, legs, ledger, claims, authorizations (steps 2-7): discovers from the settlement rule that the trip's mileage entry is missing, from the mileage rule that the lodging entry is missing. Agent explains plan-side bookings are needed -> member: go ahead. Step 9 books lodging (returns MR-261125-4414), step 11 books mileage (returns MR-261125-8057). Agent asks payment method (prepaid card) and hands over the payout with benefit reference, claim number MR-261125-8057, amount 2035.77 -> member runs collect_trip_settlement_816cec94 and reads 'paid' -> agent confirms -> member closes. Every must-ask item (identity, trip, stay, receipts, method, consent) has a scripted answer; nothing waits on the outside world.

[13] Standard solution and verification. Read rows as in steps 2-7; compute B on the opening world, write it; compute A on the world after step 9, write it; compute K on the world after steps 9 and 11, hand it over. Verification entry point: scratchpad verify.py with spec_t0.py (replays the real tools step by step and evaluates each policy's compute with the gate's own build_env/eval_compute). Output: step 0 lodging result=1811.25 (args lodging_nights 12, meal_days 13), return claim MR-261125-4414; step 1 mileage result=179.66 (approved_miles 576.8), return MR-261125-8057; step 2 settlement result=2035.77; factor baselines as in [4]; ALL-BASELINE 1235.0 / 91.73 / 1990.91; skip step 0 -> [mileage 139.78, settlement 156.18]; skip step 1 -> [settlement 156.18]. Gates run: check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools --task 0 TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK; replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (14 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous); check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK (9 base gates); check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK (14 factors, 7 cross, history rows 29, branches 40); check_grounding --task 0 GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire --task 0 SCOPE OK; check_cache_diff INFO only. check_traceability not run: the KB is not rendered yet.

[14] Revisions. (a) check_extended flagged module-level helpers in task_tools.py as undiscoverable tools -> inlined the claim-number and owner lookup into each tool -> re-run OK. (b) check_compute: history not load-bearing (only LATEST reads, which the floor test does not zero) -> the trip's route miles became SUM of the trip's registered leg miles, the edge-day share reads MAX leg miles of the trip, and the settlement entries became SUM of approved entries with the trip date; rules, compute_basis and baselines updated in the same pass -> values unchanged (1811.25 / 179.66 / 2035.77) -> COMPUTE OK. (c) The payout first carried an offset of an appeal continuation liability; dropped because recovering it would require a write to another category; replaced by the late-settlement allowance.

[15] Policy/GT closure. policy -> tool -> computation -> call -> terminal: ride_ext_stay_lodging_meals -> approve_stay_lodging_meals_3bb3a021 -> computations[0] step 9 amount 1811.25 -> ride_ledger lodging_meals row; ride_ext_trip_mileage -> approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186 -> step 11 amount 179.66 -> mileage row; ride_ext_trip_settlement -> collect_trip_settlement_816cec94 -> step 13 amount 2035.77 -> paid row under MR-261125-8057. required_documents = charter_scope.extended_policies in the same order; task_tools in first-call order.

[16] Draft recomputation from the visible context (hidden compute/GT masked): from the three rules as prose, the legs (07:45 / 14:45, 218.4 miles, radiation, registered 2026-08-31), the ledger (no RL-5541907 entry, latest lodging 2025-11-17, latest mileage 2026-08-24), the claims (ten course claims, last booked 2026-10-13), the membership (ABD, 74) and the authorization (K0001 approved): lodging 7 x 85 + 5 x 72 + 12.5 x (31 + 3.25) x 2 = 1811.25; mileage (436.8 + 10 x 14 = 576.8 -> 561.44) x 0.32 = 179.66; settlement 1990.91 + 1990.91 x 0.01 x 1.5 + 15 = 2035.77 — same as gold, one reading only.

[17] Manual values gates (task 0): length/breadth and hidden test — pass (see [8]-[9]); the in-person write is the member choosing and collecting her own payout, done on the spot. Need and simulator boundary — pass: object (September Omaha trip), timing (today), authorisation (agent books plan-side, member collects), no incidental asks. Chronology — pass: nothing volunteered that gold creates. Base eligibility and time anchor — pass (see [5]). Authoritative facts and object — pass (see [6]). Reachability without waits — pass (see [12]). Prerequisite sentences — pass (see [8]). Rule/compute equivalence — every binding quotes a rule sentence verbatim (scripted check: no unquoted binding, no non-verbatim basis); every ladder is stated in full in its rule with pairwise disjoint conditions. Factor honesty — each baseline is exactly the computation paragraph (standard nights, standard nightly and daily allowances, round trip at the standard rate, sum of approved amounts), each method factor changes how a quantity is computed (lodging night taper bands, local round trip counting, mile taper, clock anchor); the added-nights ladder is labelled a parameter because it selects a number of nights added to one expression. Self-contained dossier — this text.

[18] Round-2 rework (audit policy_task round 1). F-C1 / T0-F1: the stay computation's only method-labelled factor selected an added-night count; it is now labelled parameter (ladder values: plus two / plus one / no added night), and the nightly-rate ladder became an honest method, stay_length_lodging_taper, choosing between a three-band taper, a two-band taper and a flat pay-out (piecewise formulas over the lodging nights). The stay computation now carries 5 parameter + 1 method factors. Re-run (verify.py spec_t0.py): lodging 1811.25 (lodging part 955.00 = 7 x 85 + 5 x 72; meals 856.25), claim MR-261125-4414; mileage unchanged 179.66 (it reads the lodging entry's date and nights, not its amount); settlement 1990.91 + 29.86365 + 15 = 2035.77; per-factor baselines 1670.75 / 1876.25 / 1845.50 / 1661.25 / 1730.00 / 1383.12 (stay), 117.90 / 139.78 / 139.78 / 184.58 (mileage), 2005.91 / 2065.64 / 2025.82 / 2020.77 (settlement); all-baseline 1235.00 / 91.73 / 1990.91; skip runs unchanged (139.78; 156.18). Observations closed in the charter: O-RC-1 (one noun, 'lodging nights', in the stay rule); O-RC-2 (mileage and settlement rules now say 'the latest lodging and meals entry', as compute reads it); O-PS-1 (the mileage prerequisite sentence now applies only to multi-day trips whose one-way miles reach the lodging threshold, so a short multi-day trip is never blocked; condition and policy_source updated here); O-AB-1 (the payout's claim-number docstring no longer refers to an approval receipt).

[19] Round-3 rework (audit revision_2). F-C4 / T0-F2: the settlement clock's middle tier read the trip's registration after its outbound date, which no settled trip can meet (mileage needs registration before the appointment). It now reads the return leg's registration after the outbound date (a stay extended while away, the return leg re-registered before the return appointment), which a settled trip can meet; the clock then starts on the return leg's registration date. All three tiers are reachable; on this world the claim-booked tier is taken and every figure is unchanged (re-run verify.py spec_t0.py: 1811.25 / 179.66 / 2035.77, per-factor and all-baseline figures as in [18]). O-FL-4: the mid-drive miles moved from 100 to 150 so every edge-day tier is reachable on levels with a 120-mile lodging threshold (218.4 still takes the middle tier). O-FL-5: the regional and metro trip miles moved to 150 and 200 so the fall-through (120-149 miles) is reachable by trips that carry local round trips (218.4 still takes the metro tier). O-PG-3: the mileage->lodging condition is left as a restatement of the rule's own 'latest lodging and meals entry' wording (no different outcome).
user_scenario: You are Theodora Vance-Okonkwo, 58, calling Prairie Ridge Health Plan member services from Broken Bow, Nebraska, the day before Thanksgiving. You are soft-spoken and a little worn out from treatment, polite, and you like to understand things one piece at a time; you say 'hon' now and then. You use a wheelchair, and your husband Walt drives you everywhere in your own van, which is why your plan pays you for mileage instead of sending a car. What you want: this September you went through two weeks of radiation at the cancer center in Omaha. You registered that trip on the member portal back at the end of August, the way you always do, and for your other trips the travel money just showed up on your RideLink prepaid card a couple of weeks later. This time nothing has come, and it has been two months. You open by saying roughly that: you did your radiation down in Omaha in September, nothing has been paid for that trip yet, and you would like whatever you are owed for that trip put onto your RideLink prepaid card today. You do not know how the plan works any of it out, you do not know any amounts, and you never suggest numbers. Only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give your details, and only the ones asked for: your Medicaid ID is PR42731608 and your date of birth is May 19, 1968 (1968-05-19); if asked for your phone number it is 4025540386, and if asked for the last four of your Social Security number it is 4417. If the agent asks which trip, you say it was the radiation course at Heartland Radiation Oncology Institute in Omaha, your first treatment was Monday September 14 early in the morning and your last one was Friday September 25, and the reservation number on your confirmation email is RL-5541907. If the agent asks whether you stayed over, you say yes, you and Walt stayed at a motel near the clinic from the Sunday night before the first treatment until the morning of the last one, and drove home that Friday afternoon. If the agent asks for motel or meal receipts or amounts, you say you kept the motel receipt in a folder somewhere but you don't have it in front of you and you can't remember what it came to. If the agent asks who drove or whether anyone went with you, you say Walt drove and stayed with you the whole time because you need him for transfers in and out of the chair. Whenever the agent explains that something has to be put through on the plan's side before the money can go out, you tell them that's fine, go ahead and do whatever needs doing on their end; you do not ask what it is for. If the agent asks how you want to be paid, you want it on your RideLink prepaid card, the same card the other trips went on, not a check. When the agent hands the payout to you to do yourself, you go through it exactly as the agent reads it to you, using the reference number, the claim number, the amount and the prepaid card choice the agent gives, and then you tell the agent what your screen says. If the agent tells you an amount and it sounds higher than you expected, you just say 'oh, that's more than I thought, thank you' and do not question it. Once the agent tells you the money has gone to your prepaid card, you thank them, wish them a happy Thanksgiving and say goodbye; you do not bring up anything else.

edges.condition: The ledger carries an approved mileage entry for the trip whose trip date is the trip's outbound appointment date, and it is the latest approved mileage entry.
edges.policy_source: A trip settlement is not released until the ledger carries the approved mileage entry for that trip.

edges.condition: For a multi-day trip at or above the lodging threshold, the ledger's latest approved lodging and meals entry carries the trip's outbound appointment date as its trip date.
edges.policy_source: For a trip whose return leg falls on a later date than its outbound leg and whose one-way miles reach the level's lodging threshold, the mileage entry is fixed only after the ledger carries the approved lodging and meals entry for that trip.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The return leg (2026-09-25) is later than the outbound leg (2026-09-14) and the trip's 218.4 one-way miles reach the 120-mile lodging threshold, so the sentence applies; the only (hence latest) lodging and meals entry on the ledger is MR-251121-3309 with trip date 2025-11-17 for RL-5538842, none for RL-5541907.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Step 9 books MR-261125-4414 (lodging_meals, RL-5541907, trip date 2026-09-14, 12 nights, 1811.25 USD); stay_entry_date then equals out_date and local_trips moves from 0 to 10.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain (settlement -> mileage -> lodging and meals) with no parallel prerequisites, so the order is fixed by the two prerequisite sentences: the mileage entry is fixed only after the trip's lodging and meals entry stands, and the settlement is not released until the trip's mileage entry stands. Any other order changes a scored value (see edge_load_bearing).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Verification run skipping step 11: the settlement's entries fall back to the latest mileage entry MR-260903-2150 (139.78, trip date 2026-08-24), the lodging entry no longer pairs with it, the credit scale drops to 1 and the settlement recomputes to 156.18 instead of 2035.77; the terminal ledger also lacks the mileage entry.

Verification run skipping step 9: local_trips becomes 0 (latest lodging entry dated 2025-11-17), approved miles 436.8, and the mileage amount recomputes to 139.78 instead of 179.66; the settlement then recomputes to 156.18; the terminal ledger also lacks the lodging and meals entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only for 'whatever you are owed for that trip put onto your RideLink prepaid card today'. It never mentions a mileage claim, a lodging or meals claim, an approval, or that anything must be booked first; the motel stay, Walt's help and the receipt folder come out only when the agent asks, and her only reaction to an explanation of back-office steps is 'go ahead and do whatever needs doing on their end'. It contains no policy id.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: approve_trip_mileage_f67ba186 and collect_trip_settlement_816cec94 each look up the benefit only to copy customer_id and then call ctx.create on ride_ledger unconditionally; neither reads the ledger for a lodging or mileage entry, neither returns an Error, and both write the same row whether or not the prerequisite entry exists (the verification skip runs above wrote them without complaint).
